## Summary

Starting master SHA: `41281095348ba7ffa9d1748910ede227705d5446` (M3A + M3B, card database
facade and deck model/`.ydk` codec, both merged). Branch: `m3/fast-card-search`. Final head:
`91be4c8292d9be66e2fba046594c7446adaad378` (three rounds of external-review fixes landed
after initial open - see "Review fixes" near the end).

Addresses exactly one M3 roadmap item: **"Fast search over the full card pool"**. M3 remains
in progress after this PR - the deck builder UI is not started. Also includes one unrelated
tiny housekeeping fix, as its own first commit: README's condensed milestone table still
showed M2 as in-progress when `docs/ROADMAP.md` already correctly marks it done.

- `edopro_next::data::CardSearchIndex` (`data/include/edopro_next/data/card_search_index.h`,
  `data/src/card_search_index.cpp`): builds an explicit, presentation-independent snapshot
  from a `CardDatabase` and answers structured `SearchQuery`s with deterministic ranking. No
  Qt/QML/Irrlicht/`ocgcore`/`gframe`/`DeckBuilder`/`DeckManager`/LFList/networking.
- `SearchQuery`/`SearchResult`/`MatchKind` (`search_query.h`, `search_result.h`): a
  structured query type - text/scope, exact code, typed static metadata filters - not
  upstream's compact sigil mini-language.
- `normalize_search_text` (`text_normalize.h`/`.cpp`): source-faithful case/accent folding,
  UTF-8/`char32_t`, no locale dependency.
- A new CMake target, `edopro_next_search` (`data/CMakeLists.txt`), depending on
  `edopro_next_data` (accepted exception - searching needs card data) but never exposing
  SQLite.
- `docs/architecture/card-search.md` - full source archaeology of `DeckBuilder::
  FilterCards`/`CheckCardProperties`/`CheckCardText`/`SortList` and `DataManager::
  GetSetCode`, with exact line citations against upstream `54ea755a`.
- `docs/adr/0005-card-search-structured-query.md` - the three load-bearing decisions.
- `data/tests/test_card_search.cpp` - 35 tests, all passing.
- `data/tests/bench_card_search.cpp` - a non-gating performance measurement executable.
- `docs/ROADMAP.md`, `README.md` - status updates.

## Source archaeology findings (full detail in `docs/architecture/card-search.md`)

- `DeckBuilder::FilterCards` (`gframe/deck_con.cpp:1059-1190`) parses a compact sigil
  mini-language: `||` splits independent OR-terms, `&&` splits AND-subterms, `*` splits a
  subterm into tokens, and an optional prefix (`!!` negate, `@` archetype-only, `$$`
  text-only, `$` name-only) selects a mode.
- `DeckBuilder::CheckCardProperties` (`:1191-1324`) mixes ordinary static-metadata filtering
  (type/race/attribute/ATK/DEF/level/scale/category/link-marks) with genuine legality/policy
  in the same function: an unconditional top-of-function gate excluding tokens/hidden
  cards/non-official scope unless anime-mode or a whitelist is active, and a large switch
  consulting the loaded `LFList`'s ban/limit counts and named `SCOPE_*` legality categories.
- `DataManager`'s `uppercase_name`/`uppercase_text` (`CardString`, `gframe/data_manager.h:
  100-105`) are precomputed once at load time, never per search, and the sixteen auxiliary
  strings are **never** searched by `CheckCardText` - only name and rules text.
- `Utils::ContainsSubstring` (`gframe/utils.cpp:664-674`)'s own doc comment says "all tokens
  are contained in the input," but the implementation requires them in left-to-right,
  non-overlapping order (each token's search starts where the previous match ended) - an
  artifact of a single forward-advancing `find()`, not a stated design choice.
- `DeckBuilder::SortList` (`:1397-1432`) is a UI column sort (by level/ATK/DEF/name/passcode,
  card-type-aware), not a relevance ranking - explicitly not reproduced as this module's
  ranking scheme.
- `DataManager::GetSetCode` (`gframe/data_manager.cpp:401-421`) resolves a human, localized
  archetype-name string into numeric setcodes using a strings resource entirely outside
  `CardRecord`/`CardDatabase` - out of scope for this PR. `CardSetcodes`/`check_set_code`
  (`gframe/deck_con.cpp:1325-1340`) resolve *which* card's setcodes to check: an aliased
  card's own (usually empty) setcode is not used - its alias's is - reproduced exactly.

## Architecture chosen

An explicit `CardSearchIndex` snapshot, built from a `CardDatabase` by `rebuild()` and never
observing it afterward - a later `load_database()`/`load_locale()`/`clear_locale()` call is
invisible until `rebuild()` runs again, by design (ADR 0005, Decision 1). A simple
`std::vector<Entry>` with precomputed normalized strings, scanned linearly by `search()` - no
inverted index, no third-party search library (see Performance below for why).

## Normalization semantics

`normalize_search_text` reproduces `Utils::ToUpperChar`'s (`gframe/utils.h:320-358`) exact
Latin-1 accent-folding table codepoint-for-codepoint (À-Å/à-å etc. -> A, similarly E/I/O/U/N,
plus `¡`->`!`/`¿`->`?`), in UTF-8/`char32_t` rather than upstream's `wchar_t` - every
codepoint the table cares about fits in one UTF-16 code unit, so this sidesteps the Windows
(16-bit)/Linux (32-bit) `wchar_t` width difference without changing any result. A codepoint
outside the table (any non-Latin script, or a Latin-1 character like Æ/ß upstream's own
fallback does not touch) passes through unchanged - verified empirically that upstream's
`std::toupper` fallback, under the default `"C"` locale with no `setlocale` call anywhere in
this codebase's search path, only affects plain ASCII `a`-`z`. Implemented directly rather
than calling the locale-dependent `std::toupper`, so this never depends on the embedding
process's global locale state.

## Structured query API

`SearchQuery`: `text`/`text_scope` (`Name`/`Text`/`NameOrText`), `exact_code` (a ranking
hint - see "Ranking" below), and typed static filters, each using the operator that
actually matches its upstream source (audited individually - see "Static filters
implemented" and `docs/architecture/card-search.md`§2.1):

- `type`/`link_marker`/`scope`: `BitmaskFilter{require_all_bits}` - **all** selected bits
  must be present.
- `category`: `AnyBitmaskFilter{any_bits}` - **any** selected bit is enough (a deliberately
  different shape from the above - upstream's own effect-category filter is any-of, not
  all-bits; an explicit `AnyBitmaskFilter{0}` means no constraint, matching upstream's own
  zero-mask short-circuit).
- `race`: `std::optional<std::uint64_t>`, **exact equality** - not bitmask containment,
  matching upstream's single-value selector.
- `attribute`: exact match.
- `attack`/`defense`/`level`/`left_scale`/`right_scale`: `NumericFilter{value, EqualTo|
  AtLeast|AtMost}` - both sides compared as `int64_t`, with no narrowing back to the
  field's native width and no silent unsigned reinterpretation.
- `setcodes`: "any of these", alias-resolved.

`limit` is applied after ranking. `CardSearchIndex::rebuild(const CardDatabase&)` builds the
snapshot; `search(const SearchQuery&) const` returns `std::vector<SearchResult>` - a
`CardCode` plus a `MatchKind`, never a pointer into index- or database-owned storage.

## Text matching semantics

`text` is normalized once, then split on the full ASCII whitespace set (space, tab, CR, LF,
vertical tab, form feed) into tokens - matched with **order-independent** AND semantics
(every token must appear somewhere in the field, any order), a deliberate departure from
upstream's ordered `Utils::ContainsSubstring`, chosen because the ordering requirement there
is traceable to *how* it happens to be implemented, not to any stated intent, and because
order-independent matching is the more ordinary search-box expectation. `Name`/`Text`/
`NameOrText` scope isolation matches upstream's own `SEARCH_MODIFIER_NAME_ONLY`/`TEXT_ONLY`
behaviour. Text that is empty, or normalizes and tokenizes to zero tokens (i.e. contains
only ASCII whitespace), carries no text constraint at all - see "Ranking" below.

## Ranking

`MatchKind`, in priority order: `ExactCode` > `ExactName` > `NamePrefix` > `NameMatch` >
`TextMatch` > `NoTextQuery` (every filter-passing entry when `text` is empty *or* normalizes
and tokenizes to zero tokens, i.e. contains only ASCII whitespace - a deliberate "match
everything" contract, not "match nothing," so a caller building a browse-the-catalogue view
needs no separate code path, and a live search box that is transiently empty or all-spaces
gets the same browse behaviour without needing to trim it first). Within a tier, results are
ordered by normalized name
ascending then `CardCode` ascending - a total order, so the same index and query always
produce byte-for-byte identical output. A new scheme, informed by but not copied from
`SortList`'s UI column sort.

## Static filters implemented

Type/link-marker/scope (bitmask "require all"), category (bitmask "any of" - **not**
"require all", matching upstream's own any-of `filter_effect` semantics exactly, see
"Review fixes" below), race (exact equality against `CardRecord::race`, matching upstream's
own single-value selector - **not** a bitmask-containment filter), attribute (exact match),
attack/defense/level/left_scale/right_scale (typed numeric comparison, 3 operators),
setcodes (OR, alias-resolved). Deliberately excluded: `TYPE_TOKEN`/`SCOPE_HIDDEN`
auto-exclusion, anime-mode gate, LFList ban/limit/whitelist, named `LIMITATION_FILTER_OCG`/
`TCG`/`ANIME`/etc. categories - all legality/policy, not search
(`docs/architecture/card-search.md`§2's full upstream-filter-to-`SearchQuery`-field table).
`defense` never matches a Link monster; `left_scale`/`right_scale` never match a non-Pendulum
card - both mirroring `CheckCardProperties`'s own unconditional exclusions. A full
operator-level audit of every static filter against `CheckCardProperties` is in
`docs/architecture/card-search.md`§2.1. The "?" ATK/DEF
sentinel (-1/-2) needs no special case: a realistic `AtLeast` threshold already excludes it
via ordinary signed comparison. `level`'s M3A-established `uint32_t` wraparound representation
for a negative packed value participates in numeric comparisons exactly as upstream's own
`uint32_t` comparison would, verified directly.

## Alias/setcode decision

`setcodes` is a purely numeric filter over `CardRecord::setcodes` - schema data. Resolving a
*human archetype name* (what `@name` does upstream, via `DataManager::GetSetCode`) needs a
localized set-name string resource entirely outside `CardRecord`/`CardDatabase` today -
deliberately deferred. The numeric alias-resolution rule (`CardSetcodes`: an aliased card's
search uses its alias's setcodes, not its own) is reproduced exactly, resolved once per card
at `rebuild()` time into `Entry::effective_setcodes`, not per query.

## Locale/rebuild lifecycle

`CardSearchIndex` never observes `CardDatabase`. A `load_database()`/`load_locale()`/
`clear_locale()` call is invisible to a previously built index until `rebuild()` runs again -
tested explicitly through the full base -> locale -> clear cycle, and separately for a later
database override, both showing the pre-rebuild staleness as documented, deliberate behavior.

## Performance implementation chosen and why

A `std::vector<Entry>` of precomputed normalized strings and static metadata, scanned
linearly - no inverted index, no SQLite FTS, no third-party search library. Chosen because it
measured comfortably fast, not by default: see below.

## Benchmark dataset and measured results

`data/tests/bench_card_search.cpp`: 22,000 deterministic synthetic cards (real Yu-Gi-Oh pool
is ~13,000; this gives margin), realistic-length two-word names plus an id suffix, and rules
text built from 2-5 concatenated sentence fragments (~150-400 characters). Measured on this
development environment (WSL2/Ubuntu, g++ 15.2.0, `-O2` - one data point, not a guaranteed
number on every platform):

| Operation | Time |
|---|---|
| `CardDatabase::load_database` (22,000 rows) | ~216 ms |
| `CardSearchIndex::rebuild` (cold) | ~243 ms |
| `CardSearchIndex::rebuild` (warm) | ~250 ms |
| Exact-name query (no match - worst-case full scan) | ~6.6 ms |
| Name-prefix query (~1,100 hits) | ~6.7 ms |
| Broad text-scan query (~8,000 hits) | ~8.6 ms |
| Filtered query, no text (~8,000 hits) | ~5.6 ms |
| Ranked broad name query (~1,500 hits) | ~6.4 ms |

(Re-measured after the correction pass below - the stricter UTF-8 validator and corrected
filters made no meaningful difference; run-to-run variance on this shared development
environment is larger than the delta between the two measurements.)

Every query lands single-digit-to-low-double-digit milliseconds, comfortably inside normal UI
responsiveness budgets, with no index beyond a vector and a linear scan. On this evidence, no
inverted index, n-gram index, or third-party search dependency was added.

## Memory considerations

`Entry` copies only what `search()` needs - two normalized strings and static metadata - not
the sixteen auxiliary strings (never searched) and not a `CardRecord*`/pointer back into the
database. No further micro-optimization attempted; clarity and determinism prioritized over
saving kilobytes at this scale.

## What legacy search behavior was deliberately not copied

The `||`/`&&`/`*`/`$`/`$$`/`@`/`!!` sigil grammar itself (structured fields cover the same
capabilities, `||`/`&&` composition and `!!` negation excepted - see below); `SortList`'s
UI-column relevance model; `Utils::ContainsSubstring`'s ordered-token requirement;
archetype-*name* resolution; the upstream six-way numeric filter-type scheme (replaced with
three general-purpose comparisons).

## Explicit separation from legality

No `LFList`/banlist parsing, no ban/limit/semi-limit counts, no whitelist logic, no
"legal card" concept, no deck-size/copy-count validation, no format/duel-rule policy
anywhere in this PR. `scope` is exposed as a raw bitmask filter only - not a legality
decision this module makes. Full table of what upstream's `CheckCardProperties` does that
this module deliberately excludes is in `docs/architecture/card-search.md`§2.

## Tests: 35 (`data/tests/test_card_search.cpp`), all passing

Empty catalogue; the empty-query "match everything" contract; exact/prefix/substring name
tiers; case-insensitivity; accent normalization (both direct `normalize_search_text` checks
and an end-to-end accented-name search); Name-only/Text-only/NameOrText scope isolation;
order-independent multi-token matching; full ranking-tier ordering; tie-break by name then
code; no duplicate results for a card matching in both name and text; raw scope metadata
never auto-excluded unless explicitly filtered; the "?" ATK/DEF sentinel; Link-monster
defense exclusion and link-marker bitmask matching; 64-bit race; the wrapped-uint32 level
case; setcode OR-matching with alias resolution; the full locale rebuild lifecycle; a
database override staying stale until rebuild; repeated-call determinism; limit truncation
after ranking; and three `exact_code` cases pinning its ranking-hint-not-filter contract
(including the case that caught the wrong first implementation during development - see ADR
0005, Decision 3).

`edopro_next_data`'s 30 tests and `edopro_next_deck`'s 37 tests are unchanged and still pass.

The existing `card-database` job (id and display name both unchanged - "Card and deck data"
remains an accurate-enough description now that it also builds/runs `edopro_next_search`/
`test_card_search`, per this task's own guidance) covers the new target automatically, since
it lives in the same `data/CMakeLists.txt`/`data/build` tree. Expected jobs: Regression
harness (3.10, 3.12), Card and deck data, Semantic client model, Qt 6 shell, Upstream EDOPro
baseline (observer=false, observer=true).

## Review fixes landed since this PR opened

Three rounds of external review, all fully addressed on the current head:

- **Round 1**: `normalize_search_text` treated a malformed lead byte's raw numeric value as
  if it were itself a decoded codepoint, then folded it - 0xC3 (195), the lead byte of a
  truncated two-byte UTF-8 sequence, falls inside the fold table's own 192-197 "A" range by
  numerical coincidence, so a truncated sequence silently normalized to "A" instead of
  passing through unchanged as documented. `decode_utf8` was changed to return a bool
  distinguishing a genuinely decoded codepoint from a malformed byte, pinned by three new
  cases, bringing the suite to 28 tests.
- **Round 2** (this pass): the Round 1 fix was still only a *shape*-based check (right byte
  count, each byte a generic continuation byte), which still accepts overlong encodings,
  UTF-16 surrogates, and codepoints beyond U+10FFFF - the same class of bug, generalized.
  `decode_utf8` now implements Unicode's own canonical well-formedness table. Also found:
  `category` was implemented as "require all selected bits" when upstream's own
  `filter_effect` is any-of; `race` was implemented as bitmask-containment when upstream's
  own filter is exact equality. Both fixed (new `AnyBitmaskFilter` type for `category`;
  `race` changed to a plain `std::optional<std::uint64_t>`). Also corrected: stale
  documentation claiming `NumericFilter` values are converted to each field's native type
  (they are not - both sides compare as `int64_t`, now documented precisely and pinned by a
  new test); an over-strong "never throws" claim on `normalize_search_text`; a stale
  `CardRecord::text1` reference; a misleadingly-named test renamed to match what it actually
  proves; and a whitespace-only text query now correctly takes the same "no text constraint"
  path as a genuinely empty one. Ten new tests in this round, bringing the suite to 34.
- **Round 3** (this pass): two tiny edge cases plus wording. `AnyBitmaskFilter{0}`, explicitly
  set, was rejecting every card instead of behaving as no constraint - upstream's own
  `filter_effect &&` short-circuit means a zero mask is "nothing selected", not "match
  nothing"; fixed, with a test confirming `SearchQuery{}` and an explicit
  `AnyBitmaskFilter{0}` now return identical results. `whitespace_tokens` only recognized
  space/tab/LF/CR as whitespace, not the full ASCII set the documentation already claimed
  (vertical tab, form feed added). Also corrected two remaining stale statements in
  `card-search.md`: Ranking's `NoTextQuery` description didn't mention the whitespace-only
  case, and a claim that `type`'s positive all-bits filter could "exclude tokens" (a
  require-these-bits predicate cannot express negation - corrected to state plainly that
  this module has no negative filter). One new test, bringing the suite to 35.

## Known limitations / deliberately deferred work

- Archetype-*name* search (`@name` upstream) is not implemented - needs a set-name string
  resource `data/` does not yet represent.
- `||` (union of independent queries) and `&&`/`!!` (cross-sub-term AND/negation) have no
  `SearchQuery` equivalent - a caller wanting `||` composes multiple `search()` calls itself;
  the others are plausible small additions later, not built speculatively here.
- No compatibility parser for upstream's exact sigil grammar - considered (ADR 0005,
  Decision 2) and deferred pending an actual keyboard-parity power-user use case, since it is
  small but not trivial and would conflate two different reviews if bundled here.
- Fuzzy matching, edit distance, phonetic search, stemming, and autocomplete are not
  implemented - none of this exists upstream either.
- No asynchronous/background search - measured fast enough (see Performance) that this may
  not be needed at all; left for the eventual UI layer to decide.
